Origin Story

From Zero
to Le Mans

Born in a small Colombian town with no racetracks, Sebastian dreamed of becoming a race car driver. From age 15, he worked multiple jobs to fund a passion the world didn't yet believe in.

His trajectory was set when a young Sebastian was trained for the first time by Juan Pablo Montoya himself, who immediately recognized the raw talent. Sebastian went on to claim go-karting championships and was named best rookie in his Formula Cars debut.

Then — at the peak of his momentum — a devastating off-track accident fractured everything. Multiple injuries. Career on hold. Back to zero.

Most would stop. Sebastian rebuilt. He sold car parts, restarted from scratch, re-entered motorsport as a coach for Ferrari and Porsche Championships — and used that platform to claw his way back into competition.

"Once in a decade talent who refused to let circumstances define his ceiling."

— The Racing Community
🏆 Comeback Milestones Won multiple rounds in the Porsche Endurance Championship Brazil against world-class competition. Finished 2nd at the 24 Hours of Sebring. Now: Pole position at the 2026 Le Mans Cup opener.

Round 1 — April 2026

Barcelona
Dominance

1:42.339
#11 Aston Martin Vantage AMR GT3 EVO · Code Racing

Sebastian secured a dominant GT3 pole position at the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya, finishing 1.314 seconds clear of the nearest rival — the Ferrari #88 AF Corse. His lap time not only placed him first in class but underlined a raw pace that took the paddock by surprise.

Leading the 2-hour race before a contact retirement on Lap 6, Sebastian showed both speed and racecraft. The story is just beginning.

Round 2 — May 2026

Paul Ricard
Dominance

2:04.744
#11 Aston Martin Vantage AMR GT3 EVO · Code Racing

Sebastian secured yet another GT3 pole position at Circuit Paul Ricard, finishing 0.7 seconds clear of the field in qualifying.

In the race, Sebastian dominated the first hour, building a commanding gap of +20 seconds over second place. When handing the car to his co-driver, a technical failure forced retirement — the pace and class had been undeniable.
